{{Short description|Mathematical inequality}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Bernstein's theorem''' is an [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] relating the maximum [[Complex number#Definition and basic operations|modulus]] of a [[complex number|complex]] [[polynomial function]] on the [[unit disk]] with the maximum modulus of its [[derivative]] on the unit disk. It was [[mathematical proof|proven]] by [[Sergei Bernstein]] while he was working on [[approximation theory]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=R.P. |last=Boas, Jr. |title=Inequalities for the derivatives of polynomials |journal=Math. Mag. |volume=42 |issue= 4|pages=165–174 |date=1969 |doi=10.1080/0025570X.1969.11975954 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/0025570X.1969.11975954 |jstor=2688534|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Statement ==
Let <math>\max_{|z|=1} |f(z)|</math> denote the maximum modulus of an arbitrary
function <math>f(z)</math> on <math>|z|=1</math>, and let <math>f'(z)</math> denote its derivative.
Then for every polynomial <math>P(z)</math> of [[degree of a polynomial|degree]] <math>n</math> we have

<math display=block>\max_{|z|=1} |P'(z)| \le n \max_{|z|=1} |P(z)|</math>

and equality holds if and only if <math>P(z) = \alpha z^n</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M.A. |last1=Malik |first2=M.C. |last2=Vong |title=Inequalities concerning the derivative of polynomials |journal=Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=422–6 |date=1985 |doi=10.1007/BF02844535 }}</ref>

==Similar results==
[[Paul Erdős]] conjectured that if <math>P(z)</math> has no zeros in <math>|z|<1</math>, then <math>\max_{|z|=1} |P'(z)| \le \frac{n}{2} \max_{|z|=1} |P(z)|</math>. This was proved by [[Peter Lax]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=P.D. |last=Lax |title=Proof of a conjecture of P. Erdös on the derivative of a polynomial |journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. |volume=50 |issue= 8|pages=509–513 |date=1944 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1944-08177-9 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-50/issue-8/Proof-of-a-conjecture-of-P-Erd%C3%B6s-on-the-derivative/bams/1183506031.pdf}}</ref> More generally, if <math>P(z)</math> has no zeros in <math>|z|<k,</math> for <math>k \ge 1</math>, then <math>\max_{|z|=1} |P'(z)| \le \frac{n}{1+k} \max_{|z|=1} |P(z)|</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first=M.A. |last=Malik |title=On the derivative of a polynomial |journal=J. London Math. Soc. |volume=s2-1 |issue=1 |pages=57–60 |date=1969 |doi=10.1112/jlms/s2-1.1.57 }}</ref>
